lines.text: In winter, many Indian households make laddoos. The reason is not only that they taste good.
A laddoo is built from flour, ghee, goond, nuts and seeds. Ghee is a fat, and so are the
cooking oils in every Indian kitchen —
Fats do the same essential job as carbohydrates — they supply energy — but they do it
differently. Gram for gram, fat carries more than twice the energy of carbohydrate, and
the body stores it rather than burning it at once. Fat is stored energy: the reserve the
body draws on when food is not coming in, and part of how it keeps warm.
That is why a laddoo belongs to winter. It is dense, slow energy at the time of year
the body needs most of it.
Fats come from plants and from
animals. Plant sources include groundnut, walnut,
cashew, almond, pistachio, coconut, sesame seed, pumpkin seed, sunflower seed,
soya bean and the oils pressed from them. Animal sources include butter, ghee,
The bear that does not eat for months Before winter, a polar
bear eats heavily and builds a thick layer of fat under its skin. Through
the long winter it may eat almost nothing, living off that stored fat
while the same layer keeps it warm. Stored fat is a survival strategy,
